our patient has INAD with progressive cerebellum degeneration and auditory neuropathy.
the patient had a clinical diagnosis of infantile neurodegeneration with brain iron accumulation (IBA), with a genetic diagnosis of PLA2G6 associated infantile neuroaxonal distrophy.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the clinical phenotype of our patient with infantile neuroaxonal degeneration was expanded to include auditory neuropathy and the use of deep neuroimaging in the diagnosis of this condition.
INAD is a rare neurodegenerative disorder with a wide spectrum of clinical presentation.

our patient with infantile neuroaxonal distrophy (INAD) with novel variants of the PLA2g6 gene expands the clinical phenotype and highlights the importance of genetic testing to delineate this condition.
The main takeaway from our work is that
INAD should be considered in the differential diagnosis of patients with early onset of neurodegeneration and progressive cerebellar degeneration, even in the absence of the classic phenotype.

the use of genetic testing is important in the diagnostic work-up of neurodegenerative diseases, particularly those that have overlapping clinical features and are associated with progressive atrophy on neuroimaging studies.
INAD should be included in the differential diagnosis for patients with early infantile neuroregression, hypotonia and cerebellar atrophic changes on MRI.
